Method of Attack: Adding a counterfeit test package to the official Microsoft Azure SDK latest releases list by exploiting bot automation that picks up npm packages where the 'azure-sdk' account is a collaborator, allowing the malicious package to appear as part of the official Azure SDK suite.
Disguising malware as an official Azure SDK package to potentially enable software supply chain attacks.
Attack Vector: Publishing a malicious npm package and adding the 'azure-sdk' npm account as a collaborator to trick automated bots that update the Azure SDK releases page.
Manipulation of automated GitHub commits by the 'azure-sdk' bot to include the malicious package in the official releases CSV file.
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of the package 'alexbirsantest' on the official Microsoft Azure SDK latest releases page
GitHub commit by 'azure-sdk' bot adding 'alexbirsantest' package to the CSV file for Azure SDK releases
index.js file in alexbirsantest version 2100.4.2 containing proof-of-concept code
